summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-25. Most in-window blunders were election-administration errors, and most of those either are already on the bench (Volusia, Utah County) or were set aside earlier because they lacked a second accepted source. I'm submitting one candidate: the Bexar County, Texas, early-voting ballots that showed another district's measure in place of East Central ISD's Prop A. It was set aside on Oct. 23 only because the headline was too long. It now has a headline under 110 characters and two independent accepted sources, KSAT (Oct. 19) and TPR (Oct. 20), and both quotes were checked word for word against the fetched pages. Search capacity ran out before I found any further alternates with two accepted sources. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-25 (window Oct 19–25). The search limit was hit after about 20 searches, and no lead reached two accepted sources, so no candidates are submitted. The strongest lead is still Northwestern's single-positron trap (Physical Review Letters, Oct. 21). Northwestern's Weinberg College news page (Oct. 22) opened and confirms the result and date, but every accepted news page failed again: Phys.org (two different URLs) was 'not accessible' and Scientific American was 'not allowed'. Yale's levitated-nanoparticle result (PRL, Oct. 23) has Science News but no openable official or second page. Sports and Guinness leads (Misiorowski's World Series pitch-speed record, a Texas drone show, a Florida hip-thrust record) turned up only on non-accepted sites before the search limit was reached. No genius story met the standard; nothing published. The verified facepalm story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: Some Bexar County, Texas, early ballots show another school district's measure instead of Prop A
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: Toledo, Ohio, mayor says employee error caused chemical tank leak; evacuation orders lifted
candidates.reason: In the window (Oct. 20–23, AP via WRAL). This was an industrial tank rupture that forced hundreds of residents to evacuate or shelter in place. That makes it a hazard with affected residents, not a self-contained blunder, and injuries could not be ruled out.

candidates.headline: LA mayoral candidate Nithya Raman walks back 'gold standard' remark about former LAPD Chief Daryl Gates
candidates.reason: In the window (CBS LA, Oct. 21), but the remark is about immigration enforcement and touches on race. The rules exclude both. Only one accepted source was opened.

candidates.headline: Imperial County, Calif., mails duplicate ballots to about 160 voters
candidates.reason: In the window, but the only coverage found was the Imperial Valley Press (not accepted), Yahoo and AOL (banned) and the county's own site on a .org domain (not an accepted official domain).

candidates.headline: University City, Mo., towed about 150 cars from private property; residents sue
candidates.reason: The lawsuit's claims are contested, and the residents whose cars were towed are on the receiving end of the alleged error.

candidates.headline: Douglas County, Nev., replaces ballots
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was the Record-Courier, which isn't on the accepted list, and the nature of the error wasn't clear from the results.

candidates.headline: Tompkins County, N.Y., voting machines not working at early voting sites
candidates.reason: The only source found (14850.com) isn't accepted and couldn't be opened. No blunder by officials has been established.

candidates.headline: Pompano Beach, Fla., man arrested after nine false 911 calls about a body
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was Hoodline, which isn't accepted. The behaviour may point to a mental-health issue.

candidates.headline: Northwestern physicists hold a single positron in a controlled quantum state for months (Physical Review Letters, Oct. 21)
candidates.reason: In the US and inside the window, and Northwestern's Weinberg College news page (Oct. 22) opened and confirms the result. But no accepted news page could be opened: both Phys.org URLs returned 'not accessible', the Scientific American article returned 'url not allowed', and the PRL DOI and APS Physics pages were not accessible. The rest of the coverage (sci.news, Tech Explorist, ZME Science, Yahoo, Slashdot, Digg) is not accepted. An official page alone is not enough.

candidates.headline: Yale-linked team's levitated nanoparticle detects kicks from single gas atoms (Physical Review Letters, Oct. 23)
candidates.reason: Science News (Oct. 22) opened and confirms the result, but the PRL DOI page and APS Physics Magazine were not accessible. No Yale release turned up, so there is still only one accepted source.

candidates.headline: Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski sets a World Series record for fastest pitch
candidates.reason: Seen only on Fox Sports, which is not an accepted publisher. The search limit was reached before AP, the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel or another accepted outlet could be found, so the pitch speed and game date were not checked.

candidates.headline: Texas drone light show sets two Guinness World Records (about Oct. 21–22)
candidates.reason: Seen only on CTV News and UPI, neither of which is accepted. The city, date and record details were not checked before the search limit was reached.

candidates.headline: Florida woman sets a Guinness record with a 639-pound weighted hip thrust
candidates.reason: Seen only on UPI's Odd News, which is not accepted. It was not opened, and the date of the lift was not checked.

candidates.headline: Endogenous retrovirus DNA in chimps may help explain human–chimp brain differences (Science Advances, Oct. 23)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. According to Science News, the study is led by Johan Jakobsson at Lund University in Sweden. The finding is also hedged ('may help explain').

candidates.headline: Rise and fall of a continent-spanning cliff may explain the Grand Canyon's missing billion years
candidates.reason: Too old. Science News published it Oct. 9, before the window. It is also a hedged 'may help explain' hypothesis.
